_comment: The single source for every constant more than one runtime has to agree on.
Edit this file, then run `make generate-protocol`. Never edit a generated file.
`make check-protocol` (in `make lint`) fails when a generated file is stale.

activity_dir.doc: One marker file per in-flight speak, present for the whole synth+playback window. Polled by the menu bar app's speaking indicator and scanned by every stop path.

activity_dir_env.doc: Overrides activity_dir. Its only real use is pointing tests at an isolated directory, so they do not touch the real one or any speak in flight. The TTSCONTROL_ prefix is kept from when one package was its only reader: it is a published escape hatch, and renaming it would silently stop working for anyone who set it.

playback_lock.doc: Exclusive flock(2) held for the duration of playback, so concurrent speaks (the MCP server, hooks, the menu bar) queue instead of talking over each other. Two paths would be two locks, and both would play at once.

playback_lock_env.doc: Overrides playback_lock, for the same reason activity_dir_env exists: a test that runs a real speak takes this lock, and on the shared path it queues behind any speech in flight on the machine. Every reader honours both or neither, or an isolated test is only half isolated.

synth_pid_suffix.doc: Sidecar naming the synthesizing process, for a stop to signal.

play_pid_suffix.doc: Sidecar naming the playing process, for a stop to signal.

stopped_suffix.doc: Sidecar telling a speak a stop was deliberate, so it neither plays nor treats the cancellation as a failure and falls back to `say`.

engine_url.doc: Where mlx-engine binds. Whoever holds a stale copy either fails to bind or health-checks a socket nobody is listening on, and then reports the engine down while it is running.

engine_pid_file.doc: Written by the start script, removed by the server's own idle exit. These disagreed once, so the idle exit cleaned up a file nothing created and left the real one behind.

temp_dir.doc: Where ava puts what it produces: per-dictation audio, cleaned up on exit, and `ava monitor` transcript logs, which are kept.
